newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle backs labeling gene altered goods.
newsitem.headline: Nestle backs labeling gene altered goods.

text.p: Nestle SA said that it backed the idea of providing special labels for products that contain genetically altered substances.

"Although we see no safety or scientific justification for such labeling, we recognise the consumer interest in this information and will therefore, in addition to any legal requirements, indicate the use of ingredients produced with the aid of gene technology on the label wherever reasonable and practicable," it said in a statement.
A Nestle spokesman said this was not a new position, but that the company was expressing it more clearly than in the past.
"We've said from the very start that we want the consumer to get all the information he needs to make a decision," Nestle spokesman Francois Perroud said.

Nestle, the world's largest food company, has insisted that genetically altered soy beans are safe and of high quality and it intended to use them in its products despite protests from environmental activists.

Greenpeace demonstrators earlier this month draped a banner from Nestle headquarters in a protest urging Nestle not to use the products, which some environmentalists say are a risky experiment with nature and might pose a threat to human health.
